case_number: Criminal Appeal No 1273 of 2022 (Arising out of SLP (Crl) No 9509 of 2019)
summary: The appeal challenged the Karnataka High Court's judgment holding that ingredients of offences under Sections 405 and 420 IPC were prima facie made out against the appellant. The complaint alleged improper billing and loss of professional fees, with claims of assurance by the appellant to reimburse. The Supreme Court examined whether cheating and criminal breach of trust were substantiated. It held that the dispute pertained to a contractual obligation and termination of services; mere breach of contract without dishonest or fraudulent intent at inception does not constitute criminal offences under Sections 415, 420, or 405 IPC. No deception or fraudulent inducement was established.
legal_provisions_cited: Hridaya Ranjan Prasad Verma v. State of Bihar
Ajay Mitra v. State of M.P.
final_judgment: The appeal was allowed, and the impugned judgment of the High Court was set aside. No case was made out for criminal prosecution under Sections 405 and 420 IPC; the matter was remanded for appropriate closure of criminal proceedings.
